deck: This week, investments surge while legacy systems retire and new risks emerge.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly secured $190M in Series C funding, pushing its valuation to $1.6B. The capital will bolster its co-orbital security and space domain awareness capabilities, which are increasingly critical given the uptick in global tensions. With the DoD's focus on pull-through contracts, this funding signals a strong alignment with government priorities.
stories.soWhat: True Anomaly's cash influx highlights the increasing demand for space security solutions—just when the competition is heating up.

stories.head: Atlas 5 launches final Amazon Leo satellites
stories.body: The final Atlas 5 rocket launched Amazon's Leo satellites, marking the end of a 20-year run for the vehicle. The mission, which took place last week, underscores the transition of satellite launches from established vehicles to newer entrants like SpaceX and Vulcan Centaur. With the Atlas 5 retired, the space launch landscape is shifting dramatically.
stories.soWhat: The end of Atlas 5 signifies not just nostalgia but a stark reminder that legacy systems can’t compete forever—even in space.

stories.head: Boeing's Starliner woes linked to overconfidence
stories.body: A recent report suggests that Boeing's Starliner issues stem from overconfidence and unrealistic timelines, with the company struggling to meet its schedule. This comes as Boeing faces scrutiny over its ability to deliver on its commitments, especially with a $4.5B NASA contract at stake. The report implies that the calendar might be Boeing's toughest adversary yet.
stories.soWhat: If Boeing can't recalibrate its expectations, it risks losing more than just contracts; it could lose its credibility in the space race.

watchlist.title: FCC satellite licensing vote approaches
watchlist.body: The FCC's upcoming vote on satellite licensing could reshape the regulatory landscape, impacting how quickly companies can deploy new constellations.

watchlist.title: Anduril and L3Harris bid for SDA
watchlist.body: The collaboration between Anduril and L3Harris on a tactical SDA constellation could set the stage for future defense contracts, especially in a budget environment favoring space resilience.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser moves forward
watchlist.body: With the Dream Chaser DoD variant clearing its critical design review, expectations will rise for its first flight—let's see if it can deliver faster than its predecessors.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN extension under scrutiny
watchlist.body: Palantir's $480M extension on the TITAN ground station program will be closely watched, as government contracts increasingly favor established players over newcomers.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
